de92a0aa79bee52b09297d1042e24980f4743b56: Bad Gastein offers 82.7 km of well-marked runs, a medium-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing quite the same thing twice. The 17 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in peak season. Bad Gastein's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. Bad Gastein's altitude (1002 m at the bottom, 2300 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover through the middle of winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Bad Gastein is clearly high: 79€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short, Bad Gastein lives up to its promises: a Northern Alps resort that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.
dea315d105e7ff57188d00de756a74c51f7e371b: A resort on a human scale, Brauneck focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 31 km of runs suit a 3 to 4 day stay very well, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly find new terrain. Technical terrain reigns at Brauneck: with 22 black and 67 red runs on the programme, confirmed skiers will find plenty to test themselves. Off-piste and freeride are enjoyed there in often excellent conditions, thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. Brauneck's moderate altitude — base at 700 m, summit at 1712 m — makes it sensitive to weather variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking snow reports before you leave is strongly recommended. Budgeting for a stay at Brauneck is clearly on the high side: 53€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. That is the price of excellence — but it is worth being aware of it before you set off. In short: Brauneck doesn't rival the giants of skiing, but doesn't pretend to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
deb0fd422f5469eb875fa704d49a2ae198e73ce8: Alpe di Mera is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 17 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and lift queues that barely exist. Alpe di Mera has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Alpe di Mera's moderate altitude, from a base at 682 m to a summit at 1739 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the most reliable months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you travel is strongly recommended. At 42€, the day lift pass places Alpe di Mera in the mid-range category for budget: neither a bargain nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Alpe di Mera does not compete with the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

dec2f6bf0ee12d857e1062dd21b9c953ceee1141: Bessans is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 3 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Bessans' family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Bessans' modest altitude — starting at 1740 m, summit at 1900 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before setting off is strongly recommended. With a day lift pass at just 18€, Bessans is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget, or skiers who want to make the most of their days without breaking the bank, it is a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: Bessans does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
